newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler to invest $1.3 billion more in Detroit.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler to invest $1.3 billion more in Detroit.

text.p: Chrysler Corp. said Wednesday it plans new investments of $1.3 billion in its Detroit manufacturing facilities over the next five years.
The new spending will improve efficiency and boost production capacity, Chrysler said.
"This announcement translates directly into more jobs for Detroiters," Detroit Mayor Dennis Archer said in a statement released by Chrysler.
The automaker's chairman, Robert Eaton, said the investment was evidence of Chrysler's effort to increase capacity and improve productivity and operating efficiencies.
"This is a commitment to our workers, our facilities and the City of Detroit, Eaton said."
The investment is spread over six facilities within the city -- Jefferson North Assembly, Detroit Axle, Mack Avenue Engine, McGraw Glass, Conner Avenue Assembly, and Mt. Elliott Tool and Die.
The Jefferson plant, which produces the Jeep Grand Cherokee, will be the centrepiece of the expansion plan, with $750 million earmarked for a new body shop and production expansion.
Detroit's No. 3 automaker has seen its sales of sport utility vehicles soar. They currently make up two-thirds of the manufacturer's sales.

The Detroit Axle facility will get $300 million for new model expansion and the Mack Avenue Engine Plant will get $150 million for technological improvements, bringing the total investment in the yet-to-be-opened facility to $900 million.

The McGraw Glass facility will get $100 million for new model expansion and infrastructure, the Conner Ave. Assembly Plant will get $10 million for the introduction of the Plymouth Prowler, and the Mt. Elliott Tool and Die plant will get $3 million for infrastructure improvements.
The announcement brings Chrysler's total investment in the city of Detroit to $3.8 billion since it rebuilt the Jefferson North Assembly Plant, which opened in 1992.
The company has added 2,100 Chrysler jobs in the city since 1994, when it added its third shift at the Jefferson North facility.
Chrysler has more manufacturing workers in the city of Detroit than any other automaker.
